must_not.text: Hard rule: never edit or change the user's content (no rewriting, shortening, cutting or adding). If a change seems needed, highlight it, suggest how it could be shown better, and change nothing unless the user approves.
Never let text overflow the canvas padding on any side, or the card, box, zone or node it sits in.
Never set text above 72px: the largest style is Display/XL (72/80), even for hero titles, closing statements and big numbers.

Never make it look generic or machine-made: no gradients, glows, neon, glass or blur effects, decorative filler (blobs, orbs, sparkles, floating shapes), AI cliche imagery or icons (glowing brains, circuits, robot hands, sparkles or rockets for AI), text effects, or a coloured stripe down one side of a card. Exception: Bruce AI content may use the Bruce AI gradient and glow.
Never use a colour that is not a design-system token, and never sample or approximate one.
Never use a font other than TASA Orbiter (headings) and Inter (body).
Never use in-between font sizes: text comes from Role/* or the defined text styles.
Never put a pill radius on a card, panel, container, input or image.
Never place an eyebrow on container/secondary or container/tertiary (it fails contrast).
Never show a process, workflow, lifecycle, timeline, architecture or set of numbers as a grid or row of text cards: draw it in its content form (a flow, loop, timeline, diagram, stat row or chart).
Never stretch a card or panel to fill a row or the slide when its content is short, leaving empty boxes. Size it to its content; if the slide looks empty, raise the type a role or grow the visual.
Never highlight a card on a dark slide with a dark blue fill (brand/800 to brand/1000): it disappears into background/inverse. Use container/brand with text/on-brand.
Never draw a fake product screen or dashboard. Place the DASHBOARD_MOCKUP_<NAME> placeholder and tell the user.

avoid.text: Avoid using the accent colours (accent and accent-2 together) on more than roughly 10–15% of the piece; it is a highlight, not a palette.
Avoid text/tertiary for essential text; at 3.4:1 it is for large or non-essential text only.
Avoid giving every section the same card design. Repeat a design only where the content repeats, such as a set of like items in one row or grid.

Avoid template layouts: the same icon, title and text card in every section, an icon on every heading or card when it adds nothing, or every section centred. Every element carries content or structure; when in doubt, leave it out.

design_direction.text: Slides use the three themes (light, dark, brand). If the user asks for other colours, use them, but only design-system colour tokens.
AI slides have no default theme: ask the user whether they want them dark; otherwise pick the theme for the slide like any other.
Highlight key words with text/link on light, text/accent on dark and text/accent-on-brand on brand slides, within the shared accent budget.

Start from the reference slides: the page breaker, closing, team and product stack ship as ready HTML (fill only the page breaker and closing slots; team and product stack are used as they are); normal content starts from the content-slide references, adapted to the user's content. The team slide is the leadership team; a project team is designed from the user's content.
Q&A slides use the page breaker reference slide (the brand team's mapping of "Reference Slides for QnA"): its ready HTML on background/brand with text/on-brand and the white logo top-right.
Pick spacing by purpose: gap/inline between adjacent items, gap/stack inside a component, gap/grid between cards, padding/container inside cards, padding/section between sections.
Cards and panels use the container default with a 12px corner: container/primary, 1px border/container, radius/3xl (12px), padding/container. Nest with container/secondary, then container/tertiary.

Design each section's cards for its content. The named cards are starting points; when none fits, build a new card on Card base: pick a tone, then arrange atoms, controls and text roles in its slot with spacing tokens (for example number-led, image-led, split, stat row, steps or comparison). Cards in one row or grid share one design; vary the design between sections.

Make slides infographic-led. Before designing a slide, name the shape of its content (sequence, lifecycle, phases, problem and solution, numbers, comparison, architecture, like items, people) and draw it in the matching form from content_forms: flows and timelines with connectors, loops for lifecycles, splits for contrasts, stat rows and charts for numbers. Cards are for like items side by side.
Headings use text/heading, body copy text/body, eyebrows text/eyebrow.
Show status with the five intents (Positive, Negative, Information, Neutral, Primary) and their fixed fill/text pairs; warnings use Negative.

Colour follows meaning: problems, risks and pain points use the Negative intent (red container tint, red heading or icon), not only a red chip; objectives, outcomes and solutions use brand or Positive.
Keep surfaces flat; use Low Raised only to lift a card off the canvas.
Buttons have softened square corners (radius/default), never pill.

Give each item in a list or grid of tools, capabilities, features, steps or outcomes a Lucide icon that names it, coloured with a text token that suits the surface. No decorative or AI cliche icons, and no icon on a heading when it adds nothing.
If the content is too much for the space, do not squeeze it below the minimum size or cut it: tell the user, and offer options (split across slides or pages, a different layout, a table or chart).

Fill the content area with content, not empty boxes: size cards to their content, give every block of text a container with padding/container or the same breathing room on the grid, and when a slide has little content raise the type a role and grow the visual. On covers and hero slides the title, subline and details form one group.
A label and its text sit on one line or share a first baseline, labels never wrap, and left edges line up across a slide.

Architecture, data-flow and integration slides use the architecture diagram language: zones, the four device styles with icons from the architecture icon library, arrows, colours and the I/O Sense outcome when the diagram ends in I/O Sense, scaled into the slide with text at 14px or more.
Slides about what a product shows (an I/O Sense screen, a dashboard, an operator view) use the light theme with a dashboard mockup placeholder beside the user's points.
